sources.source_file: The MicroArray Quality Control (MAQC) project shows inter- and intraplatform reproducibility of gene expression measurements - PMC.html
sources.source_route: Owner-saved PMC full-text HTML; private-literature/pmc/ outside the repository
sources.supported_claim: Intra- and intersite reproducibility and interplatform agreement of differential-expression comparisons on standardized human reference RNA.
sources.scope_and_limits: The principal A/B contrast used strongly separated reference RNAs. Gene filters, quality exclusions and platform differences matter; its agreement is not a threshold for weak biological contrasts or cyanobacterial baseline equivalence.

excerpts.location: Results: Intraplatform data repeatability and reproducibility, #P15 (PMC3272078)
excerpts.quote: intrasite repeatability and the intersite reproducibility
80% or more between platforms and 90% within platforms
greatest differences among the four sample types

sources.source_file: Comparison of the transcriptional landscapes between human and mouse tissues - PMC.html
sources.source_route: Owner-saved PMC full-text HTML; private-literature/pmc/ outside the repository
sources.supported_claim: The reported broad human/mouse tissue analysis clustered by species on its first three principal components.
sources.scope_and_limits: The same paper reports tissue-dominated structure on PCs 4–6 and on PCs 1–3 for a selected tissue subset. This original result alone does not establish a biological cause or resolve sequencing-batch confounding; the memo retains the separately cited reanalysis.

excerpts.location: Gene Expression Is More Similar Among Tissues Within a Species Than Between Corresponding Tissues of the Two Species, #s1 / Figure 1A (PMC4260565)

excerpts.quote: more tissue-dominated clustering for principal components 4–6
we obtain tissue-specific clustering in the first three principal components

sources.source_file: A new statistic for identifying batch effects in high-throughput genomic data that uses guided principal component analysis - PMC.html
sources.source_route: Owner-saved PMC full-text HTML; private-literature/pmc/ outside the repository
sources.supported_claim: Unguided PCA can miss a batch effect below the dominant variance; gPCA supplies a permutation test using a prespecified batch indicator.
sources.scope_and_limits: Known batch labels are required. Phenotype and batch were generated independently in the simulations; the application studies measured CNV. For this project, a signal aligned with study labels cannot establish a technical cause when study and condition are confounded, and supplies no calibrated RNA-seq comparability cutoff.

excerpts.quote: if the batch effect is not the greatest source of variation
gPCA is dependent on knowing how to define potential batch effects

sources.source_file: Selecting between-sample RNA-Seq normalization methods from the perspective of their assumptions - PMC.html
sources.source_route: Owner-saved PMC full-text HTML; private-literature/pmc/ outside the repository
sources.supported_claim: Normalization assumptions are method-specific; their violation can bias downstream expression analysis.
sources.scope_and_limits: The review defines expression as mRNA/cell and notes that assumptions change for mRNA/transcriptome. Library-size scaling needs constant total mRNA/cell for the former target; distribution/testing methods use balanced expression and common technical effects. A majority of unchanged genes is not a universal requirement: symmetric changes can retain performance. Controls have their own assumptions.

excerpts.quote: each condition has the same amount of mRNA/cell
There is roughly symmetric differential expression across conditions
